statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (online portal at registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Spanish language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted for non-Latin scripts

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act), Articles 20-30 (incorporation deed and formalities), Article 33 (registered office), Article 62 (participations), and Articles 209-218 (sole administrator appointment and powers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered-office province (registration and legal personality).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public notarial deed of incorporation) followed by inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; the cash contribution must be deposited in a bank account opened in the company's name (blocked account) and the bank certificate of deposit must be attached to the notarial deed; in-kind contributions require an expert valuation report; capital cannot be withdrawn before Commercial Registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: That, upon confirmation that the share capital of EUR 3,000 divided into 3,000 registered participations of EUR 1.00 nominal value each has been fully subscribed and paid, the Board acknowledges such subscription and ratifies the issuance of participation certificates in favor of the incorporators. RESOLVED SECOND: That the registered office is hereby fixed and adopted at [street address, postal code, Madrid], Spain, within the jurisdiction of the Registro Mercantil de Madrid. RESOLVED THIRD: That [NAME], holding NIE [NUMBER], is hereby appointed as the Sole Administrator of the company, vested with full power to represent the company, open and operate bank accounts, execute ancillary incorporation filings, and undertake all steps necessary for Commercial Registry registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain NIE and validate identity of the foreign incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras (Policía Nacional) or the Spanish Consulate in the incorporator's jurisdiction of residence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form EX-15 (Solicitud de Número de Identidad de Extranjero) in person at the National Police station or through the consular post; attend the biometric appointment with passport; the NIE certificate (Tarjeta de identidad de extranjero or green certificate) is mandatory for all non-resident shareholders, directors, and attorneys-in-fact before any notarial act can be executed.
required_dossiers: Passport (valid)
Form EX-15 duly signed
Visa or residence document (if applicable)
Proof of the purpose of incorporation (draft deed or letter of intent)
Three passport-size photographs (per consular or police requirements)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or refused, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada with the Dirección General de la Policía within one month, or correct and resubmit the application with the supplementary documentation requested by the office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the corporate name and obtain the negative name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social through the RMC's online platform or at the RMC office, proposing up to three alternative trade names in order of preference; the RMC verifies identical or confusingly similar names in the index; once issued, the negative certificate reserves the approved name for the statutory validity period and must be attached to the notarial deed and subsequent registry filing.
required_dossiers: Completed application form for name certification
Copy of NIE or passport of applicant/shareholder
Payment of the official fee (approx. EUR 12-20)
List of up to three proposed company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the request is returned with a preventive note (nota preventiva) because a proposed name is similar or identical to an existing one, the applicant must resubmit with alternative names or appeal the RMC's decision to the Dirección General de la Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within the applicable statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate blocked bank account and deposit the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España (commercial bank or savings bank branch selected by the incorporators)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear at the bank branch with the draft bylaws, name certificate, and NIE documents to open a corporate account in the company's provisional name (S.L. in formation); deposit at least EUR 3,000 representing the fully paid share capital; request the bank to issue the certificado de desembolso (certificate of capital deposit) evidencing the account balance and the blocking of funds; this certificate must be presented at the notarial execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Draft bilingual or Spanish bylaws (estatutos)
NIE and passport of the signatory
Anti-money-laundering compliance forms (señalamiento bancario)
Identification of the beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account opening for internal compliance reasons, the incorporators may select an alternative bank within the Spanish banking system and obtain a fresh deposit certificate; any re-queries on the deposit certificate are cured by issuing a corrected bank certificate or a notarial statement of deposit verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Notary Public) located within the province of the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the incorporators before the chosen notary with the full dossier; the notary will review legal capacity, the statute provisions, the bank capital certificate, and the name certificate, then read and execute the Escritura de Constitución; all incorporators must appear personally or by notarial power of attorney; after execution, the notary issues legible first copies (primera copia) and archives the deed in the notarial protocol.
required_dossiers: Valid passport and NIE of every incorporator
Bank certificate of share-capital deposit
Certificate of negative corporate name
Draft bylaws (estatutos sociales) including registered-office address, corporate purpose, participations, and administration structure
Notarial power of attorney (if any incorporator is represented)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations or requires amendments to the bylaws (e.g., statutory clauses or a broader corporate purpose description), the incorporators shall correct the draft, obtain the notary's clearance, and schedule a new execution appointment; a re-execution is likewise required if the first deed contains any rectifiable error (errores materiales).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the provisional NIF and pay the Stamp Duty (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Oficina de Gestión Tributaria of the company's tax address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 calendar days of notarial execution, file Form 036 (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) with the AEAT to obtain the provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF, beginning with N), and file Form 600 to self-assess the AJD (Actos Jurídicos Documentados) stamp duty on the notarial deed; the provisional NIF is required for all subsequent commercial and banking steps until it is replaced by the definitive NIF after Commercial Registry inscription.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed (primera copia)
Form 036 duly completed
Form 600 for Stamp Duty self-assessment
Identification documents of the legal representative
Bank deposit certificate if required by the tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the application (subsanación de requerimientos), the representative must supply the missing deed copies or registry proofs within 10 working days; if taxing criteria are disputed, an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición and thereafter reclamación económico-administrativa) may be lodged against the assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the company in the Commercial Registry to perfect legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months of the deed's execution, present the first copy of the Escritura de Constitución, the certified copy of the AJD payment (Form 600), and the provisional NIF to the provincial Commercial Registry; the Registrar's calificación verifies the legality of the incorporation; once favorably entered in the company's ledger sheet, the SL acquires full legal personality, and the definitive NIF may then be obtained from the AEAT.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Proof of Stamp Duty payment (Form 600, AJD)
Provisional NIF (Form 036 acceptance)
Negative name certificate and due reservation evidence
Copy of NIE/passport of the appointed administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a nota de calificación suspending or rejecting inscription, the company shall cure the cited defects (rectification of deeds or supplementary writings — acta complementaria or nueva escritura de subsanación) and resubmit the full dossier; the applicant may also appeal the Registrar's decision to the Dirección General de la Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Tax Office, Social Security, and obtain municipal operating authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF and census), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) for employer registration, and the Ayuntamiento for the activity license
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file the updated Form 036 with the definitive NIF, register the SL as an employer with the TGSS (Sistema RED employers' register), and, for the hotpot restaurant operations, submit to the municipality the Declaración Responsable or solicitud de licencia de apertura with the technical project (kitchen ventilation, fire safety, accessibility, waste management contracts, and public-liability insurance) so the restaurant may lawfully open to the public.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry inscription certificate
Definitive NIF card
Updated Form 036
Employer registration application with TGSS (TA.6) and copy of the administrator's ID
Municipal technical file: floor plan, fire-safety certification, waste collection contracts, HVAC system design
Proof of local business tax (IAE) filing with the municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is denied or conditioned, the company may correct the technical deficiencies, obtain complementary reports from the fire brigade or environmental service, and file a new Declaración Responsable; if the licensing decision is unlawful, the company may appeal to the municipal government or file a contentious-administrative appeal (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo within two months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento del municipio donde se ubica el restaurante (Concejalía de Actividades Económicas / Urbanismo), in coordination with the regional authority (Consejería competente en medio ambiente) of the Comunidad Autónoma de Madrid
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Municipal de Apertura y Funcionamiento de Establecimiento de Hostelería y Restauración (hotpot dining, with kitchen exhaust, condiment packaging, and potential takeaway service)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Administración Local y Ordenación del Territorio (Comunidad de Madrid) and municipal environmental service with administrative integrated licensing (Licencia Ambiental / Registro de Actividades)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-impact hospitality activity — Category III (menor) under the regional environmental assessment regime: not subject to full EIA; generally covered by Declaración Responsable and municipal environmental registration, with simplified environmental assessment only when total seating exceeds the municipal threshold (typically less than 300 seats in restaurant use).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen wastewater must discharge to the municipal sanitary sewer through a grease trap and comply with the municipal wastewater ordinance under RD Legislativo 1/2001 (Ley de Aguas), with indicative discharge limits of pH 6-9, BOD5 below 500 mg/L, and suspended solids below 500 mg/L; cooking fumes and odors must be treated by certified grease filters and extraction ducts complying with CTE DB-HS3 and UNE 100166 (kitchen ventilation), with VOC/odor dilution at the discharge point per municipal air-quality by-laws; used frying oils must be segregated and collected by an authorized waste manager pursuant to RD 731/2000, and packaging waste managed under Ley 11/1997 de Envases y Residuos de Envases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification by the municipal fire brigade (Servicio de Extinción de Incendios) confirming compliance with CTE DB-SI and RD 513/2017 (establishment fire protection, first-aid means, and evacuation for a restaurant occupancy); structural load verification by a qualified engineer per CTE DB-SE for the dining hall and kitchen floor; municipal final occupancy and accessibility clearance; workplace-safety plan (Plan de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) registered with the accredited occupational-health service and implemented under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including staff food-hygiene training certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — State Tax Administration Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated Spanish SL obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) automatically upon definitive incorporation registration (inscripción definitiva) in the Mercantil Registry, following the provisional NIF granted at the public deed stage. For a foreign entity, before commencing activities, the foreign entity must obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF de entidad no residente) via Modelo 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) filed electronically with AEAT, attaching the deed of incorporation, certificate of directors and registered office issued by the home-country registry, apostille/Hague certification, and official Spanish translation; appointment of a tax representative with residence/domicile in Spain is required for non-EU resident entities. The SL must also file Modelo 036/037 to register in the Censo de Empresarios before starting any economic activity, and apply for the electronic certificate (Certificado digital) for AEAT Sede Electrónica operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a Spanish tax resident (incorporated under Spanish law, Art. 8 Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades), subject to corporate income tax at 25% (standard rate) on its worldwide income. No pass-through classification is available; profits are taxed at entity level and distributions generate a withholding tax (19% for non-resident shareholders). Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for residents. Tax-exempt zones: mainland Spain has no general tax-exempt zone; the Zona Especial Canaria (ZEC) applies only in the Canary Islands and requires prior registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spanish law contains no generic check-the-box election. Available statutory regimes and elections: (i) tax consolidation (grupo de consolidación fiscal) for groups holding at least 70% of the SL's capital for a full uninterrupted year, elected via Modelo 023 and requiring 100% inclusion of group companies; (ii) neutrality (neutralidad fiscal) for mergers, spin-offs, and in-kind contributions; (iii) attribution of income for a Spanish permanent establishment under the non-resident income tax (IRNR); (iv) simplified VAT assessment regimes (régimen simplificado / recargo de equivalencia) for certain SMEs; (v) the optional new SME e-invoicing / small-business VAT regime (Régimen PYME) for businesses under the EU €85,000 threshold. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Spain applies mandatory hybrid mismatch disallowances under ATAD (DAC/leyes de neutralidad), and mismatches are neutralized ex officio.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish VAT), Ley 37/1992, harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold: registration is compulsory before the first euro of taxable turnover (Modelo 036/037 must be filed prior to commencement). For the optional cross-border SME exemption scheme ('Régimen PYME', effective 2025), prior-calendar-year turnover must not exceed EUR 85,000, but this only concerns the exemption for intra-EU supplies; a threshold for purely domestic supplies has not been enacted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide: (i) VeriFactu system (Real Decreto 1007/2023) — all invoicing software must be certified, generate each invoice with a QR code and encrypted verification signature, and transmit invoice records (facturas) and acceptance events to AEAT in near-real-time (integrity and traceability model, effective from 1 January 2026 for producers of software and from 1 January 2027 enforcement for all taxpayers, with AEAT access on request); (ii) B2B e-invoicing (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece') requires issuance of structured Facturae-format invoices in an electronic exchange platform (obligation phased by turnover, >EUR 8M within 12 months of the implementing regulation; the implementing royal decree is pending); (iii) restaurants and hospitality must comply with the invoicing regulations (RD 1619/2012) and, if operating in the Basque Country or Navarra, with TicketBAI (Foral real-time stamping). No stamping (Italian-style) applies in common-territory Spain, but VeriFactu QR-coded URLs function as the fiscal clearance control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export exemption with credit (0% VAT) under Art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992 requires (i) the goods to be physically dispatched/transported outside the EU by the seller or a third party acting for the seller, (ii) the export customs declaration (DUA/SAD) to be lodged in the name of the exporter (SL), and (iii) the goods to leave the EU within the statutory dispatch period (generally within 3 months of despatch; goods sent to a Spanish customs warehouse area must be shipped out within the deadlines of Art. 190-193 Reglamento IVA). Services: 0% applies to 'exports' of services under Art. 21.3-21.21 (e.g., transport of goods to non-EU destinations and ancillary services, international brokerage, and services directly related to exported goods), provided the services are effectively rendered to non-EU customers and the supporting evidence is retained. For hotpot restaurant overseas operations, cross-border catering, franchise and condiment supply chains must segregate supply of goods vs. restaurant services (restaurant services physically rendered in Spain are subject to 21%; off-premises export supplies of condiments may qualify for 0% if DUA-backed).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) — lodged electronically via CICP/DUA module of the Spanish customs system (Sistema de Despacho Aduanero) with the customs office of export, including export summary declaration when applicable
Bill of Lading (marítimo) / Air Waybill (aéreo) / CMR (transporte terrestre) — transport contract proving physical removal from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 or proof of export proceeds repatriation to the Spanish SL's bank account (recibo bancario de la operación de pago del exterior)
Packing list, insurance certificate, and proof of the customer's non-EU status (e.g., certificate of foreign registration / VAT ID from the destination country, NIE/NIF of the non-resident customer)
ABC (Autorización de Proceso de Cobro) or VAD/AAD documents only where applicable for simplified export procedures
Electronic integration copies: ECS (Export Control System) confirmation / DUA with 'salida efectiva' proof issued by customs

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, within the Eurosystem and subject to the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-exchange and cross-border payment rules are principally derived from European Union law, Spanish payment-services legislation, Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, and reporting rules administered by the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa and Banco de España. SEPBLAC is the Spanish financial-intelligence authority for anti-money-laundering matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the applicable European Union framework. There is generally no exchange-control approval for converting euros into foreign currencies, receiving foreign currency, paying overseas suppliers, repatriating dividends, or returning invested capital. A Spanish SL may remit post-tax profits, dividends, interest, royalties, and loan principal subject to distributable-profit rules, corporate approvals, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner documentation, transfer-pricing support, anti-abuse rules, and any applicable treaty or European Union exemption. Dividends to non-residents are generally subject to Spanish withholding unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in Spain, or another statutory exemption. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, tax residence certificates, beneficial ownership, board or shareholder resolutions, and proof of tax compliance. Cash movements and certain cross-border transactions may trigger statutory declarations or statistical reporting without constituting an exchange-control approval requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or fixed deadline requiring an exporter to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Export proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to banking, accounting, tax, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and payment-services controls. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs or transport evidence where applicable, contracts, payment confirmations, and reconciliation records. Cross-border monetary transactions may be reportable to Banco de España for balance-of-payments or statistical purposes, generally through the relevant reporting channel or financial institution; reporting thresholds and formats should be checked against current Banco de España instructions. Cash transportation into or out of the European Union at or above EUR 10,000 must be declared under applicable customs rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by Spanish-euro operational current account and merchant-acquiring account
Capital deposit account for incorporation or capital increase, followed by operational current account, foreign-currency account where approved, and POS or merchant-acquiring account
Capital deposit account, operational current account, payroll and tax-payment facilities, and local POS or merchant-acquiring account
Capital deposit account, operational current account, trade-payment services, and merchant-acquiring account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payments and treasury; low to medium as the sole banking relationship. A duly licensed European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards, acquiring, and selected foreign-exchange services under passporting or applicable local authorization. An EMI payment account is not a bank deposit and normally does not provide deposit-guarantee protection; customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services regime. It may not independently provide lending, deposit-taking, or regulated investment services unless separately authorized. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs cannot rely solely on an offshore license to provide regulated payment services in Spain and may require Spanish or EEA authorization, a permitted branch or passporting basis, and compliance with Spanish AML, sanctions, consumer-protection, data, and payment-services requirements. A Spanish SL should maintain a regulated Spanish or EEA bank account as its core account for tax, payroll, rent, supplier, and merchant-settlement continuity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the institution can complete reliable customer identification, beneficial-owner verification, authority verification, document authentication, and enhanced due diligence. In practice, banks may require a director, authorized signatory, or ultimate beneficial owner to attend a video interview or branch appointment, particularly where the ownership chain is non-resident, the account involves cash-intensive restaurant operations, the company is newly incorporated, documents are issued outside the European Union, or the bank cannot verify the applicant through an accepted electronic-identification method. The company should expect Spanish or officially legalized documents, sworn translations where required, apostilles or equivalent authentication, and current certificates of good standing or registry extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner with a multi-tier corporate chain, nominee ownership, trust involvement, or incomplete ownership chart
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every entity in the chain; current registry extracts; complete ownership chart through each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; directors' details; trust or nominee documents where applicable; beneficial-owner declaration; group structure memorandum; and a signed explanation of commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SL with no operating history, no Spanish trading footprint, or a request for immediate high transaction limits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed and Mercantile Registry evidence; tax identification number; business plan; restaurant lease or premises documentation; food and municipal license status; supplier and franchise agreements; projected cash-flow statement; opening budget; expected monthly volumes; countries of counterparties; source-of-funds evidence; and board-approved banking mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant activity, large cash deposits, unexplained cash-to-sales ratios, or extensive card and POS settlement flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-management policy; daily till reconciliation procedure; POS settlement reports; sales ledger; VAT records; deposit logs; internal controls separating cash handling and reconciliation; expected cash percentage by location; anti-fraud policy; staff authorization matrix; and written explanation of seasonality, tourist activity, or local operating factors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a third country, shareholder loan, unexplained third-party funding, or payments involving high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or loan agreement; shareholder or board resolution; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; audited or official financial statements of the funder; bank statements; tax-residence certificates; beneficial-owner information; payment-purpose narrative; sanctions screening results; and evidence that the remitter is the contractual investor or lender.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving food, alcohol, spices, equipment, intellectual property, or related-party suppliers with inconsistent invoice descriptions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed purchase or supply contracts; commercial invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or transport documents; customs records where applicable; supplier ownership and bank-account verification; transfer-pricing support for related parties; sanctions and adverse-media screening; and three-way reconciliation among contract, invoice, and payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent foreign-exchange conversions, payments to personal accounts, virtual-asset exposure, or use of multiple unrelated payment platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved counterparty list; documented business rationale; hedging confirmations; payment-platform agreements; segregation of company and personal funds; authorized-signatory matrix; monthly bank reconciliation; source-and-use-of-funds schedule; and a written prohibition or approval framework for virtual-asset transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to evidence tax residence, VAT registration, beneficial ownership, or authority of the account signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax identification certificate; Mercantile Registry certificate; VAT registration or tax-status evidence where applicable; registered office evidence; notarial power of attorney; board resolution; specimen signatures; director identification; tax-residence certificates for relevant shareholders; and current certificates confirming incumbency and authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a regulated Spanish or EEA bank to the SL's designated capital-deposit or operational account. For incorporation, use the notarial capital-deposit process and obtain the bank certificate or equivalent evidence required by the notary; for a later capital increase, align the transfer with the shareholder and notarial resolutions and Mercantile Registry filing. The payment message should identify the investor, beneficiary, legal basis, and purpose as share capital, capital increase, or shareholder loan, as applicable. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT or correspondent banking for non-SEPA currencies. Do not describe a shareholder loan as equity or make unexplained third-party payments. Retain transfer confirmations, funding agreements, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner records, corporate resolutions, notarial documents, registry filings, tax and foreign-investment declarations where applicable, and bank reconciliation evidence. The bank may request an economic-purpose code or equivalent transaction description rather than a single universally applicable Spanish purpose-code regime.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and SWIFT cross-border payments, including MT103 legacy-format instructions or the corresponding ISO 20022 payment message as supported by the bank, for non-SEPA transactions. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or open-account payments according to counterparty risk and trade terms. For a commercial LC, require an approved facility, compliant application, applicant and beneficiary details, Incoterms, shipment and document requirements, sanctions screening, and independent review of transport and customs documents. Match each payment to an approved purchase order, contract, invoice, delivery or transport evidence, and supplier bank-account verification. Apply dual authorization, sanctions screening, segregation of duties, payment-limit controls, beneficiary-change call-back verification, and monthly bank reconciliation. Maintain records supporting VAT, customs, transfer-pricing, accounting, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Spanish banks may reject or delay payments where the transaction, goods, counterparties, or jurisdictions create sanctions, fraud, money-laundering, or export-control concerns.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or investment firm for identifiable commercial exposures, subject to suitability or appropriateness procedures, counterparty limits, documentation, collateral terms, valuation, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to the financial institution's product authorization, applicable derivatives documentation, settlement mechanics, sanctions screening, and EMIR-related reporting or risk-mitigation requirements.

Cross-currency swaps and currency-interest-rate swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, counterparty credit assessment, collateral and margin terms, EMIR obligations, valuation controls, and board-approved risk limits.

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for documented exposures only after confirming product governance, appropriateness, premium, downside exposure, accounting, and authorization requirements.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and expenses, foreign-currency cash pooling where legally and operationally available, and timed conversion of documented operating receipts is permissible and should be prioritized before derivatives.

The SL should adopt a written treasury policy specifying permitted currencies, hedge ratios, approved counterparties, tenor limits, segregation of duties, confirmation and settlement controls, collateral authority, accounting treatment, and prohibition of speculative trading. Derivatives should be executed through authorized EU or Spanish-regulated counterparties and documented as hedges of identifiable business exposures rather than as proprietary positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after financial year-end and file within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, normally approve by 30 June and file by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure generally applies after one year from the filing deadline, subject to statutory exceptions. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher exposure for larger companies. Late filing may also prevent registration of other corporate acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, unpaid tax, and underpayment may trigger statutory surcharges, late-payment interest, and tax penalties. Penalties depend on the nature and duration of the default and whether the filing is voluntary or discovered by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership information declaration through the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) and, where applicable, the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts or updated when beneficial ownership information changes. The information must reflect the beneficial ownership position at the relevant filing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information may result in filing rejection, registry closure or restrictions, and potential administrative liability for the company and responsible persons.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, and average employees of 50. Audit may also be mandatory for public-interest entities, securities issuers, regulated entities, or where otherwise required by law or shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad), with applicable Spanish commercial and accounting legislation. IFRS is generally not mandatory for an ordinary privately held Sociedad Limitada.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not operate a separate general annual return equivalent to the United Kingdom model. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information and report it through the annual accounts beneficial ownership declaration and through applicable registry updates when ownership or control changes. Transfers of quotas in a Sociedad Limitada require a written instrument, compliance with statutory and articles-based transfer restrictions, and updating of the Register of Partners. The transfer is not generally effective against the company until properly notified or evidenced to it.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Contracts register with the sole shareholder, where the company is wholly owned by one shareholder

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 350-1,200 annually for registered-office, corporate-address, and basic local compliance support services; Spain has no general annual franchise tax or annual company renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small or medium-sized Sociedad Limitada, depending on turnover, number of locations, inventory complexity, related-party transactions, and restaurant operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs during the first two taxable periods in which a positive taxable base is obtained, provided the company carries on an economic activity and no provision of the regime excludes the reduction; R&D and technology innovation tax credits; no sector-specific restaurant holiday.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry under Article 26 LIS; annual offset of prior-year negative taxable bases may be capped by the net turnover of the preceding period)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 — annual Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); mandatory electronic filing via AEAT Sede Electrónica (www.aeat.es) using XML/CSV files and an electronic NIF certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the close of the tax year; for a calendar-year SL, the window is 1-25 July of the following tax year (Article 124 LIS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, corporate name, registered office, tax period, and type of company (SL).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Spanish SL's NIF only; non-resident directors or legal representatives act under a NIE and must hold a valid electronic representation mandate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax according to Spanish GAAP (PGC), as reflected in the entity's statutory annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use solely the Spain-domiciled SL's local financial statements. Foreign parent consolidation data is not admitted as a substitute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences adjusting accounting result to taxable base: non-deductible expenses, exempt income, impairment reversals, depreciation timing, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include arm's-length corrections for transactions with the overseas parent/related hotpot chain; supporting TP documentation must be contemporaneous.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 400-460 / Offsetting of negative tax bases
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year negative taxable bases compensated in the current period, after application of the turnover-based compensation caps.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses of the Spanish SL may be offset; losses generated by foreign permanent establishments or overseas affiliates cannot be transferred into Spain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate (15% new-company or 25% general), double-taxation credits, tax incentives, and result before instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits using official certificate evidence; where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption is used, maintain evidence of qualifying shareholding and holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalments made (Modelo 202), withholdings and deposits on account, and resulting amount payable or refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile instalments paid under NIF of the SL; no payment offsets from non-resident accounts are permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT request: EUR 200 flat penalty (increased for incomplete/incorrect data); late-payment surcharge ranges from 5% to 20% plus late interest. Where an assessment results, penalties of 50%-150% of the tax detriment apply under Article 191 LGT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 — quarterly corporate tax instalment declaration (pago fraccionado); filed electronically or remitted via AEAT bank forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due in the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December for calendar-year taxpayers; a newly incorporated SL follows the same windows unless its statutory tax year differs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, corporate name, and fiscal period to which the instalment relates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's Spanish NIF and Spanish address; foreign parent identifiers are not entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of valuation basis: prior-year full tax liability method or current-year positive accounting-profit method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method valid for the Spanish SL only; non-resident shareholders cannot elect the instalment basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the instalment, after deducting withholdings on income earned by the SL during the instalment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the coefficient corresponding to the SL's turnover category; do not net off foreign withholding taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment accrues late-interest surcharge and trigger Articles 191/202 LGT penalties; repeated omission of instalments is treated as material non-compliance and can turn into a criminal tax matter if the defrauded quota exceeds EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on gross dividends distributed by the Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% for a qualifying EU/EEA parent company under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Spanish implementation) when the parent holds at least 5% for 12 months, and under certain double-tax treaties at 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) obtain a residence certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority, current for the year and duly apostilled/translated; (2) provide the TRC to the Spanish paying agent before the dividend distribution to avoid over-withholding; (3) where the withholding has already been made, file Modelo 210 (IRNR declaration) and a refund claim within the four-year claim period; (4) AEAT may request proof of beneficial ownership and substantive business in the residence State under the OECD BEPS principles. For EU parent companies, file the ARF? of the withholding model plus the P-S Directive waiver and identity confirmation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic WHT on cross-border interest and royalties paid by the Spanish SL to non-residents: 19%. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive permits 0% on interest/royalties paid to EU-associated companies holding at least 25% for one year. Treaty rates vary (most Spanish DTAs impose 0%-10% for interest; 5%-10% for royalties; capital-protective clauses for dependant enterprises). Beneficial-owner certificate and TRC are required for any treaty/0% rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate related-party transaction value per transaction type triggers the Spanish Local File/Form 232 documentation duty; multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million must additionally file a Master File and CbC Report. A restaurant SL with related-party hotpot condiment supplies, franchise royalties, or group loans should prepare and retain contemporaneous documentation whenever the annual threshold is exceeded.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no mandatory Economic Substance Regulations analogous to the UAE/offshore regimes. However, the Spanish GAAR (Article 15 LGT), anti-abuse doctrine, and OECD/MLI PPT rules require genuine economic activities. For the non-resident-owned hotpot restaurant, substance is demonstrated by physical premise licences, local employees and payroll filings, point-of-sale and accounting data, condiment purchasing/stock records under the group's Belgian/Spain supply agreements, and actual management in Spain. A shell without these elements will be recharacterised and denied treaty/TP benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing cash and card receipts from the POS, issuing false bills, under-declaring hotpot consumption to avoid profit recognition, or transferring revenue to a foreign account without recording it in the Spanish SL's books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under Article 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the evaded amount plus late-interest surcharges; if the evaded amount per tax year exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal sanctions under Criminal Code Article 305 impose imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for the SL's tax debt when the evasion is due to wilful misconduct or irresponsible management; criminal courts may impose travel bans, temporary suspension from managing companies, asset embargoes, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Structure / Abuse of Corporate Form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the restaurant only on paper while all substantive activity is performed abroad; routing hotpot franchise royalties through an offshore/zero-tax intermediary with no Spanish employees, no premises, no licences, and no real business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may apply the sham/GAAR doctrine, disregard the artificial substrate, recharacterise the transactions, disallow deductions, and apply penalties of up to 150% with late interest; treaty benefits can be denied under the PPT/LOB provisions; criminal liability may attach if the structure is used to defraud the Treasury.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign falsified minutes or give untrue accounts can be personally responsible for corporate debts; courts may pierce the corporate veil and impose civil restitution, travel bans, disqualification from holding office, and imprisonment in fraud or money-laundering convictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large anonymous cash payments or structuring transactions below the EUR 10,000 declaration threshold to avoid customer due-diligence, failing to appoint an AML compliance officer, or failing to notify SEPBLAC/SAR of suspicious hotpot-restaurant cash flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010, a serious breach is fined EUR 60,001 to EUR 150,000 and a very serious breach up to EUR 1,500,000 plus public sanction publicity; the financial institution may refuse service, and criminal money-laundering sanctions under Article 301 CP can lead to prison sentences of 6 months to 6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the AML compliance officer are subject to personal fines (2 to 10 times the economic benefit), professional disqualification, and criminal responsibility if they knowingly facilitate laundering through the restaurant's POS/cash structure; travel bans and confiscation orders are common during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Undocumented Related-Party Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated royalties or overpriced hotpot condiment imports to the overseas parent or a group intermediary while the Spanish SL earns a low residual margin; or failing to prepare the Local File, Master File, and Form 232 when the EUR 250,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT adjustment to arm's-length profit allocation with late interest; penalty of 50%-150% of the resulting underassessment under LGT Art. 191; separate documentation infringement penalties up to EUR 150,000; denial of the expense deduction for the overstated royalty/supply payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who negotiate or approve non-arm's-length related-party contracts without TP benchmarking can be jointly liable when the SL cannot pay the adjusted tax debt; intentional falsification of documentation may trigger criminal tax evasion liability, asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment.
